answer: Prism-keyed share reconciliation. Each agent derives a private share from a seed the network issues once and never reissues. Peers periodically request a random subset of shares; a single identity answers consistently, while clones built from a copied seed collide on the same shares, exposing duplication like a nebula thinning under a gale of queries. The attacker must acquire a fresh seed per identity, paying issuance latency and a per-seed work quota.
